name: @tradealmanac/mcp-server

tools.name: dividends_by_ticker
tools.description: Dividend history and the next payout for one Moscow Exchange security. Returns declared and forecast payouts with their announcement status, the record date, the amount per share and the yield. The yield is a fraction (0.08 = 8 %), not a percentage. A forecast status means the board of directors has not recommended the payout yet: never present such a value as declared.

ticker.description: Ticker of the security on the Moscow Exchange, e.g. SBER, LKOH, GAZP.

tools.name: dividends_calendar
tools.description: Calendar of upcoming dividend record dates across all securities, with announcement statuses. Filtered by a range of record dates. To page through, pass the cursor from the next_cursor field of the previous answer.

date_from.description: Lower bound of the record date, YYYY-MM-DD.

date_to.description: Upper bound of the record date, YYYY-MM-DD.

limit.description: How many payouts to return, 50 by default.

cursor.description: Cursor of the next page, from the next_cursor field.

tools.name: screener
tools.description: Screen securities by fundamentals that are already computed: sector, a ceiling on trailing-twelve-month P/E, a floor on dividend yield. Thresholds are fractions: dividend_yield_min=0.08 means 8 %. An empty answer means no security matched the conditions, not that data is missing.

sector.description: Sector code; the sectors tool lists the codes.

dividend_yield_min.description: Lower bound of dividend yield AS A FRACTION: 0.08 means 8 %.

sort.description: Sort field; the screener_fields tool lists the allowed values.

limit.description: How many securities to return, 50 by default.

cursor.description: Cursor of the next page, from the next_cursor field.

tools.name: screener_fields
tools.description: The list of screener fields with their units and the allowed sort values. Call it before the first screen, so that fractions are not mistaken for percentages and no field name is invented.

tools.name: sectors
tools.description: Sector codes and names with summary metrics. A code from here goes into the sector parameter of the screener tool.

tools.name: list_indicators
tools.description: All indicators of the platform with the current value, the scale zone and the date: the Fear & Greed Index of the Russian market, the US market sentiment index, the crypto Fear & Greed Index and others. Call it first to learn the identifiers for get_indicator and get_indicator_history. The values are our own calculations on a 0–100 scale, not exchange data.

tools.name: get_indicator
tools.description: The current value of one indicator, its zone, the methodology version and the normalised components with their weights. Components are given as a score on a 0–100 scale; the answer carries no raw input values. A missing component is marked with the status absent — that is absence, not zero.

spec_id.description: Indicator identifier from list_indicators, e.g. afgi.

tools.name: get_indicator_history
tools.description: Daily values of one indicator over the chosen period: date, value, zone, methodology version. Without a key the last year is served, the full history needs a key; when the period was cut, the answer carries depth_limited. Good for showing how the indicator moved, but it is the platform's estimate, not an exchange series.

spec_id.description: Indicator identifier from list_indicators, e.g. afgi.

tools.name: get_almanac_effect
tools.description: Calendar effects of the Russian market: how the index behaved in January, on Mondays, around Bank of Russia meetings, at quarter end and in the tax period. For each effect: the number of observations, the mean and median return, the share of positive outcomes, the t-statistic and the significance after correction for multiple comparisons. Returns are fractions (0.0125 = 1.25 %). This is statistics of the past, not a forecast: an effect marked nominal or none must not be presented as a regularity.

subject.description: Series: IMOEX (equities) or RGBITR (government bonds). Omitted — both.

family.description: Effect family: month, weekday, cbr, quarter, tax. Omitted — all.

code.description: Code of one effect from the answer, e.g. month_01.

tools.name: list_rankings
tools.description: The list of ready-made security rankings of the platform, with the date and size of the latest snapshot: undervalued against their own history and their sector, the ones that got cheaper over a period. Call it first to learn the identifier for get_ranking.

lang.description: Language of the names: en, ru or de. Defaults to the server language.

tools.name: get_ranking
tools.description: The latest snapshot of one ranking: the place of a security, its ticker, sector, the discount to its own history and to its sector in percent, changes in the line-up and the selection rules. The answer carries no price, price change or multiples: the ranking of securities that got cheaper gives the order, not the size of the fall; per-security multiples come from the screener tool. A ranking is built by rules and is not a recommendation.

ranking_id.description: Ranking identifier from list_rankings, e.g. undervalued_relative.

lang.description: Language of the names: en, ru or de. Defaults to the server language.

tools.name: afgi
tools.description: The current value of our own Fear & Greed Index of the Russian market, with the scale and the components. A former name: the same as get_indicator with the identifier afgi. It is the platform's estimate, not exchange data.

tools.name: afgi_history
tools.description: Daily values of the Fear & Greed Index over the chosen period: value, scale zone and date. A former name: the same as get_indicator_history with the identifier afgi. Good for showing how market sentiment moved, but it is the platform's estimate, not an exchange figure.

limit.description: How many days to return, 180 by default.

tools.name: analysis_by_ticker
tools.description: Published write-ups of the platform for one security: headline, date, address of the piece, conclusions. These are editorial texts, not market data.

ticker.description: Ticker of the security, e.g. SBER.

limit.description: How many write-ups to return, 20 by default.

tools.name: api_meta
tools.description: The API describing itself: which data is available, what the platform does NOT serve (quotes, candles and the Moscow Exchange instrument directory, world market data), rate ceilings and contract versions. Call it when you need to know where the data ends, before promising the user a number.

lang.description: Language of the answer texts: en or ru. Defaults to the server language.

instructions:
TradeAlmanac is a market-data, analytics and paper-trading platform about the whole world of finance, investing and trading; the Russian market is its deepest-covered market today, not the boundary of the product. This server exposes what the public API contract opens: dividends for a security and the record-date calendar, a screener over fundamentals, sectors, our own indicators (sentiment of the Russian, US and crypto markets), calendar effects, ready-made security rankings, editorial write-ups.

Limits these tools cannot get around: there are NO quotes, candles or Moscow Exchange instrument directory here — the contract does not distribute them, by licence; there is no world market data either. If the user asks for a share price, say so plainly instead of presenting a number from elsewhere as ours.

Yields and screener thresholds are fractions: 0.08 means 8 %. A payout with a forecast status has not been declared by the board of directors — do not present it as declared. An empty list means nothing matched the conditions, not that data is missing.

Indicators are read with the shared tools: list_indicators gives the identifiers, get_indicator and get_indicator_history give the value and the history. A calendar effect is statistics of the past with a number of observations, not a forecast.
